---
title: Quickstart
description: Connect your agent to Valet, start a session, and hand the join code to your customer.
---

Your agent connects to Valet in one of two ways:

- **The skill**, for any agent with a shell that has `curl` and `jq`. Everything the agent must know is in one skill file, which it follows step by step.
- **The MCP connector**, for agents without a shell. Valet is verified with ChatGPT and Claude only. It may work in other MCP clients, but they are untested.

## 1. Connect your agent

### With the skill

Save the skill where your agent looks for skills. Any other agent can read it straight from [`https://valet.davidsling.in/agent/skill.md`](/agent/skill.md).

<InstallSkill skill="https://valet.davidsling.in/agent/skill.md" mcp={false} />

If the skill changes, Valet tells your agent when it starts a session, and the agent updates its copy.

### With the MCP connector

Add this URL as a custom MCP connector in your agent's settings:

```text
https://valet.davidsling.in/mcp
```

The connector offers the same tools as the skill, and Valet holds the session's token for you. It has been verified with ChatGPT and Claude only. Other MCP clients are untested, so if your agent has a shell, use the skill.

## 2. Ask for a session

Tell your agent what you need, in your own words:

```text
Start a Valet session with Acme's customer to find out why the app crashes on launch.
```

The agent starts a session with your name and a one-sentence purpose. The customer sees both before deciding, so make the purpose plain and specific.

## 3. Send the link to your customer

The agent ends its turn with a link and a code, for example:

```text
https://valet.davidsling.in/j/ABC-123
```

Send it to the person whose Mac it is. The link opens the Valet app, or shows where to download it (macOS 13 or later). The code works once and expires after 10 minutes.

Only the person at that Mac can let your agent in. Never approve anything for them.

## 4. Let the agent work

Once the customer starts the session, your agent carries on by itself. It waits while the customer answers a prompt, and tells you what it is waiting for.

- Requests the customer allowed up front run straight away.
- Anything else waits for the customer to allow or deny it on their Mac.
- A denial is final for that request. The agent finds another way within what's allowed, or asks you.

## 5. End the session

The agent ends the session when it's done and tells you what it found and changed. The customer can also end it at any time. Either way, every permission is revoked and the session's programs are stopped.
